To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) in the presence of heterogeneity, the income elasticity of aggregate budget share is a function of the heterogeneity distribution, (b) the income elasticity of an aggregate budget share converges to the exponential parameter of the density of the heterogeneity scaling factor when the heterogeneity factor support becomes infinitely large, (c) the exponential density parameter of the heterogeneity density is the income elasticity of a budget share in a model of heterogeneous agents with homothetic preferences.

the Pareto distribution is the only bounded distribution with a finite mean, and with a finite variance if it has finite support, that is compatible with the homothetic preferences scaling hypothesis.

(i) the Pareto distribution of heterogeneity factors is the only distribution of homothetic preferences that can be used in the analysis of the aggregate budget shares and income elasticities of sub groups of commodities, (ii) the aggregate income elasticity of budget shares of a sub group of goods is the same for all subgroups of commodities, and (iii) the aggregate income elasticities of the budget shares of a group of commodities are the same as that of the Pareto density of heterogeneity factors
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the income elasticity of aggregate budget shares in a competitive framework when individual agents have heterogeneous behavior, described by a bounded Pareto distributed "homothetic preference scaling factor" in the population.

the effects of behavioral heterogeneity in the population on the aggregate income elasticity of a budget share, and the conditions under which the latter is locally increasing with the medium range of incomes.
the study of a class of heterogeneous agents with homothetic preferences, and the aggregate demand functions that arise in such a setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Pareto distribution, with a large support, is a very good approximation to a large variety of heterogeneous behaviors, and that it is the most natural one to be used in the study of aggregate income elasticities of budget shares.

, in the limit from small to large incomes, the income elasticity of a budget share of a commodity is equal to the income elasticity of its individual budget share, which is equal to the elasticity of the individual demand function.

behavioral heterogeneity" is a key determinant of aggregate income elasticity of expenditures, and the Pareto distribution of homothetic scaling factors is a convenient way to model such heterogeneity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the limit of infinitely large population, aggregate expenditures income elasticities are the same as those for the individual agents, when the latter have the same income.

, in the limit, the Pareto density of the heterogeneity factors is the aggregate elasticity of budget shares with respect to incomes, and that this density is the elasticity of the aggregate demand with respect to the mean income of the population, in the case of homothetic preferences.

the aggregate behavior of a population of agents having the "same" preferences and the same income, is not always the same as that of the average agent in the population, and may even be different for different ranges of income.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aggregate income elasticity of a budget share is not a property of the commodity itself, but depends on the distribution of preferences and the size of the economy.
the aggregate budget share of a commodity is not a good proxy for the budget share of a representative consumer, when the population is heterogeneous in its preferences for that commodity.

the income elasticity of a group of commodities can be very large, even if the income elasticity of individuals is very small, and that this can be compatible with a Pareto distribution of the scaling factor of the homothetic preferences.
